newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse seen consolidating, eyeing U.S.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse seen consolidating, eyeing U.S.

text.p: Germany's DAX index was expected to continue to consolidate below the 2,700 point level as the weaker dollar put pressure on prices.
Dealers said Wall Street and data out of the U.S. would provide direction for the week. "I expect further consolidation between the 2,660 and 2,680 point level," said one dealer.
The IBIS DAX index, which reflects all-day computerised dealings in 30 leading shares, traded down 25.51 marks, or 0.94 percent, at 2,677.82.
The market was slightly off earlier lows after Wall Street opened modestly firmer.

"Export stocks are suffering from a weaker dollar," said one trader. The dollar dropped below the 1.51 mark level after the country's six leading economic research institutes said German interest rates may need to rise if money supply growth remained above target levels.
Several dealers said they were not sure what would be the market's next step and suggested a larger downward correction could still be necessary if the market was to make any real advances.
But they said direction could come from the U.S. for the rest of the week as a stream of data is released.
They also said a public holiday in parts of Germany on Friday could limit trading volume.
